# BOOK: Betty Wales, Junior (Margaret Warde / Edith K. Dunton), Penn Publishing 1906

## Front matter
- Introduction: Betty's circle from Freshman/Sophomore years at Harding College. Freshmen at Mrs. Chapin's: Katherine Kittredge (jolly), Rachel Morrison (steady), Roberta Lewis (shy), Eleanor Watson (beautiful, not general favorite), Helen Adams (forlorn), Betty Wales. Mary Brooks = sophomore then, now senior. Madeline Ayres ("Bohemia, New York"), Dora Carlson (Eleanor's devoted "freshman"), Miss Ferris (faculty friend). Story by Margaret Warde.
- Illustration list includes: "TOSS IT OVER, PLEASE," SAID MADELINE; "GEORGIA AMES DOESN'T CUT," SAID MADELINE; IT CERTAINLY WAS NOT ENGLISH; THE GIRLS WORKED VALIANTLY; HE WAS THE FIRST ONE TO SEE HER; AT THE DOOR OF HELEN'S ROOM SHE HESITATED; THE NASSAU PARTY MET BY MARY'S HAMMOCK.

## Characters (key)
- **Betty Wales**: heroine; junior; single room in Belden; "Power Behind the Throne"; cousin **Lucile Merrifield** (freshman, tall, straight hair) gets T. Reed's place (roommate Theresa Reed, married in Philippines, fake). Betty's family: father Mr. Wales (Will is brother, Nan sister, "Little Sister" youngest, smallest sister), mother Mrs. Wales. Parents go to West Indies; Betty's father telegraphs, takes party to Nassau.
- **Mary Brooks**: senior, "Argus" editor, president of The Merry Hearts; near-sighted; "penniless Miss Brooks"; mocks Roberta.
- **Katherine "K." Kittredge**: canvas bag, basketball, astronomy; can't afford trip; stays with Rachel.
- **Rachel Morrison**: class president (junior); tutors conditioned freshmen; stays home from Nassau; lives at little white house.
- **Madeline Ayres**: "Bohemian"; French song; biology/mushrooms; invents **Georgia Ames**; can graduate early; "second self."
- **Roberta Lewis**: writes; Georgia's real author; idol of Mary; father "always says yes."
- **Helen Chase Adams**: prides on knowing everyone; Philosophical Club; wrote Mrs. Erasmus J. Ames letter; becomes Argus editor (business/literary).
- **Babbie Hildreth, Babe (Baby) Parker? (Babe), Bob Parker** = "the B's" (Babbie, Babe, Bob). Bob = basketball, toads, grasshoppers, ghost in clock tower, rescues library fire. Babe: lace handkerchief, Nero jokes. Babbie: chafing-dish with copper rabbits, junior usher dress; dress reform.
- **Nita Reese**: sophomore/junior, aunt post-card incident, Hilton House.
- **Eleanor Watson**: outsider since sophomore Argus story scandal; Dramatic Club resigned; Dora's benefactor; joins Merry Hearts (end of ch. XVII); cousin Jim; step-brother ill; Aunt Flo in New York; Judge Watson.
- **Dora Carlson**: father hurt hand, barn burned; Merry Hearts' Japanese tea raised money; Eleanor paid board.
- **Georgia Ames**: fictitious freshman invented by Madeline; Merry Hearts' creation. Poems/stories in Argus (Roberta wrote "Song of Sleep" and story). Mrs. Erasmus J. Ames (Helen's letter). Tom Alison (Yale, sends violets, Huyler's, composite photo), John Alison (older brother, railroad engineer, Tombstone, Arizona; sent photo to Dr. Eaton with forged letter).
- **Dr. John Elliot Eaton**: new associate professor of English; cold; ten-minute tests; brilliant; later admits to honorary membership; "I have a particular reason"; engaged to Ethel Hale; leaving Harding; Nassau voyage.
- **Ethel Hale (Miss Hale)**: faculty, teacher (Harding); Betty's friend; sitting-room; engaged to Dr. Eaton; "John"; will live in New York; book by Eaton.
- **Miss Stuart**: registrar. **Miss Raymond**: theme course teacher. **Miss Ferris**: faculty friend. **Dr. Hinsdale**: psychology professor. **Professor Jones**: botany. **Mrs. Kent / Miss Andrews**: house faculty. **Miss Ray**: quiet freshman. **Miss Case**: rich shy junior, lonely. **Christy Mason**: junior, Japanese cousin; Argus editor. **Lotta Gardner**: usher, mother sick. **Alice Waite**: two men for Glee concert (Tom Alison). **Emily Davis**, **Marion Lustig**, **Jean Eastman** (critic), **Nora Carleton** (Argus), **Marion Lawrence (Laurie)**, **Jane Drew**, **Jane Ellis**. **Dr. Hinsdale**. **Irish maid Annie** (Belden House). **Henry** night-watchman. **Martha** (Grant's Town). **Philip Charles Augustus Smith** (fort guide, Nassau). **Janitor** (Irish, Madeline's double).

## Plot by chapter
**I**: Mary and Betty in Betty's single (Belden). Lucile arrives. Katherine, Roberta, Rachel arrive. Madeline sits on pillow. Lucile gets T. Reed's place. Betty to Mary: "fun of college."
**II**: Clan. The Merry Hearts formed in Room 27 Belden, named by Roberta. Mission: make others happy. Mary: Student's Aid Fair idea. Babe, Babbie, Bob, Helen's Philosophical pin. Madeline's rabbit party (cheese, crackers, chafing dish).
**III**: Dr. Eaton's English Essayists class; ten-minute tests. Madeline writes under Georgia Ames. Second self conversation. Belden dance; Bob catches toads and grasshoppers at Hilton House.
**IV**: Madeline tells Roberta about Georgia. Roberta submits Georgia's Arnold paper to Argus via Mary (poem "Song of Sleep" rejected). Mary reads story; Madeline/Roberta conspire. Mary humbled.
**V**: Mushroom party (inky drippers, puff-balls, meadow mushrooms). Georgia proposed as member; "Power Behind the Throne" nickname for Betty.
**VI**: Georgia's coming-out: cards (Babbie), violets (Bob, $3.80, senior from Westcott), Nita's post-card ("Georgiana Arms"), Mary's Waldorf note, Babe's handkerchief to Eaton, Helen's letter to Mrs. Erasmus J. Ames; Eaton's reply.
**VII**: Dora cries in library; Eleanor pays board; Mrs. Tait's waitress job; Betty suggests Merry Hearts entertainment; Eleanor's amendment; Japanese tea (Roberta's Japanese play; Christy Mason pays three admissions; Professor Jones); $100 for Dora; Dora's pin from Bob.
**VIII**: Faculty party at Belden; Dr. Eaton mistakes Betty for Georgia; Roberta describes Georgia; Alice Waite and Tom Alison; Tom Alison sends Huyler's, Yale prom invitation; composite photo; Ethel walks with Eaton.
**IX**: Georgia's cut problem; note from Eaton to Georgia; Merry Hearts fake Georgia's illness/Arizona pneumonia; Tombstone; Eaton's cold attitude; Betty goes to Tombstone story; Bob's photo.
**X**: Christmas at Cleveland; Mr. Wales plans West Indies; Tom's letter reveals John Alison sent photo + forged letter from Tombstone; Betty confesses to Eaton; Eaton forgives, makes Merry Hearts honorary members; "Miss Stuart".
**XI**: Janitor's ghosts, Bob's ghost prank (night-watchman catches her); Miss Stuart honorary member; Miss Case invited; Ethel crying (Betty and Madeline see); Nassau invitation (Mr. Wales' letter: Nassau, B.I.; Easter); Ethel agrees to chaperone.
**XII**: Preparations; Eleanor invited to Nassau; Marion Lawrence reports Eaton going to Nassau; fire in Main Building library; Bob leads book rescue; night-watchman "You done noble, Henry." Extra week granted.
**XIII**: Departure from Harding; Eaton on ship; Nassau: Betty's father meets; divers (Penny), Grant's Town, fort; orange-blossoms from Eaton.
**XIV**: Grant's Town, roses 3 pence, orange grove, Easter tree (Roberta's idea); oranges rolled for pennies; Ethel and Eaton lost, come back late.
**XV**: Hero plot; Hog Island; Betty nearly drowns; Eaton rescues; Ethel says "John."
**XVI**: Return; Madeline hints Eaton/Ethel; Eleanor not member; prom; Eleanor withdraws from Dramatic Club.
**XVII**: Helen Adams Argus editor; Eleanor's supper; Eleanor joins Merry Hearts.
**XVIII**: Ethel's al fresco supper invite; Babbie's junior usher dress; dress reform (simple life); Ethel and Eaton engaged; Ethel leaving.
**XIX**: Eaton will move to New York; Madeline may graduate early; commencement; donor (Eaton? fifty thousand dollars) gives $50,000 to college via dress-reform principle; Georgia Ames "found" (real freshman, dark, stout, braid, father Edward, mother dead); song "Here's to Betty Wales"; ends.

## Key quotations
- "Hello, Betty Wales. Please amuse me." (opening)
- "Toss it over, please," said Madeline.
- "Georgia Ames doesn't cut," said Madeline.
- "Then Georgia must die." (Roberta)
- "Bob Parker, of all persons, championing Eleanor's cause!" (Bob later votes Eleanor in)
- "The trouble with this novel... hero can't seem to get any chance." (Mary)
- "I can't thank you enough, John." (Ethel)
- Mary's novel title: "As It Might Have Been; or, More Than Half True."
